messages:
alex.k: Hey security — just got an email that says my 'Redwood KMS team' needs me to re-authenticate. contains a link: https://redwood-secure[.]tools/update?user=alex.k :eyes:

alex.k: Subject: "Action required: KMS access verification"
alex.k: It asks to sign in with SSO and shows a Redwood logo, but sender is "support@redwood-ops[.]cloud".

sec-bot: Incident intake created: INC-2025-315. Phishing label auto-applied. Please tag responder. :rotating_light:

jamie.ops: @alex.k thanks — can you paste the full headers or forward the raw email to phish@redwood? do NOT click the link again.

alex.k: forwarded raw to phish@redwood (just did). headers excerpt below:
```
From: support@redwood-ops.cloud
To: alex.k@redwood.ai
Subject: Action required: KMS access verification
Received-SPF: fail (mailfrom) identity=mailfrom; client-ip=198.51.100.23; envelope-from=support@redwood-ops.cloud;
DKIM-Status: none
Message-ID: <CA+abc1234@mail.example>
```

maria_s: good call forwarding. i'm pulling the link in a VM sandbox now. sharing the sandbox job id when done.

jamie.ops: also can we check if any service principal/APIs touched KMS or any suspicious Decrypt/Encrypt in CloudTrail for alex.k or related service accounts in the last 24h? if so we may rotate affected keys.

maria_s: sandbox job S-8421 queued. command used:
```
curl -s -L -I 'https://redwood-secure.tools/update?user=alex.k'
```

maria_s: Sandbox result (S-8421): landing page is credential-phish-hosting.com redirect -> form that POSTs to a different domain. no malware, purely credential harvest. SPF/DKIM checks fail. domain registered 3 days ago.

jamie.ops: summary: credential-harvest attempt, sender spoofed, infrastructure ephemeral. No evidence yet that keys were exfiltrated because alex didn't click, and alex did not enter creds.

nicole: recommend the following actions:
- Block domains: redwood-secure.tools and the credential-phish-hosting domains at email gateway and egress DNS.
- Add sender to spam filter/suppression lists.
- Run CloudTrail query for any Decrypt/GenerateDataKey or IAM token creations for alex.k and any service accounts in last 48h.
- Force session logout for alex.k (SSO) and require reauth.
- Communications: small note to employees tomorrow about this phishing vector and a reminder not to click SSO links; include screenshots.

jamie.ops: +1. i'll run the CloudTrail/OKTA session check now. also enabling DMARC enforcement rule for inbound mail to help reduce spoofing.

maria_s: blocked domains at perimeter and email gateway at 12:18 UTC. added to internal 'phish-block' list.

nicole: CloudTrail query: no KMS Decrypts attributable to alex.k or his sessions in the last 48h. OKTA: we see a new session created for alex 2 hours earlier from his usual office IP, no concurrent logins from odd locations.

nicole: still recommend rotating tokens for any short-lived API keys exposed in the last 7 days as a precaution; also run a quick secrets-scan on PRs touching infra repos.

alex.k: I did NOT click. thanks all. Appreciate the quick triage.

jamie.ops: action items captured in INC-2025-315: blocked domains, forwarded evidence to Abuse, sandbox report attached, CloudTrail + OKTA checks, session invalidation for alex. will keep open 72h for follow-up.

sec-bot: INC-2025-315 updated: status=mitigated, severity=low, owner=jamie.ops. Next review due +72h.

maria_s: for post-incident: propose an internal phish blurb + 90-sec reminder video focusing on SSO link hygiene. we can also add an email gateway rule to rewrite suspicious SSO links to show original domain as a banner.

nicole: agreed. i'll draft the comms and coordinate with comms/legal for wording. thanks team. :lock:
